and remember burnout: no job is so important you can't be offline for a few days, and "you're never as good as your best game or as bad as your worst"
data.name: End states, tagging, intent artifacts, biweekly bets

guidelines: Treat the LLM as the substrate of every interaction rather than a feature behind a button (expect hundreds of inference calls in a session and design for it)
compress context asynchronously and non-blockingly so the hot path never waits on housekeeping
run long-lived sub-agents that share context instead of monolithic per-request calls
load skills progressively rather than front-loading capability
generate UI dynamically as part of the interaction loop (show/hide the map on request) instead of pre-building every screen
make conversational voice a first-class modality, not an accessibility layer
and orchestrate all of it in real time — the patterns Gradient Bang exists to exercise
data.name: Build software with inference at the core, not bolted on

guidelines: Chunk by code structure (functions/classes/methods), never arbitrary windows
run meaning-based and exact-word search together and fuse results — they patch each other's blind spots (semantic misses exact names
lexical misses synonyms like login vs sign-in)
compress hits to name + description before sending
index call-graph edges so a hit brings its connected code
score-gate every result and send nothing below threshold — no bad context beats more context
keep everything local (privacy + speed) and prefer a small fast model for indexing — speed over perfection
share one index and persistent memory across all coding tools
instrument per-query would-have-sent vs sent × model price so savings are measured, not estimated
data.name: Build a local retrieval layer for AI coding tools

guidelines: Target "mini production": database, API services, tools, and files must match production closely enough that the agent cannot tell it is in a simulation, without running full production per experiment — think of it as an integration test rig
Snapshot the database rather than pointing at the live one
run sidecar containers for API services, databases, and MCP tools next to the agent's main container
mock API services where fidelity isn't needed
replace the human with a simulated user (an LLM with its own prompt and context mimicking real interaction) since a real user can't be in a repeatable task
For long-horizon work spanning hours, make the task multi-step: a separate prompt and separate verifiers per step, with the option to end the run early once the agent is clearly failing
Express the whole thing in the standard layout (instruction.md + Dockerfile/Compose visible
oracle solution and verifiers hidden
metadata) so tasks are portable
data.name: Build the environment as mini-production, not production

guidelines: Top-down: domain experts enumerate the entities, relationships, and properties (the '80s expert-systems method)

Bottom-up: mine entities/relations from customer interactions and grow the graph incrementally — graph databases let you attach a property or relationship without restructuring, unlike relational schemas
Reuse existing public taxonomies before inventing: schema.org, FOAF (social), Dublin Core (bibliographic), DBpedia (backs Wikipedia)
Treat "ontology" as just a graph data structure plus side-car semantics
data.name: Build ontologies top-down, bottom-up, and second-hand

guidelines: Stop waiting for better models — audit the overhang instead, comparing what frontier models achieve in your harness against baseline, and invest where the gap is engineering

mix modalities per task — cheaper models for simple pages, code generation for repeatable flows (intercept and replay network requests rather than re-clicking), CLIs like Playwright given skills and context
give agents memory and per-website skills so nothing is discovered twice, and compress page context rather than dumping raw DOM into the model

run on consistent rendering infrastructure — identical layout, viewport and environment every run — because inconsistent rendering produces inconsistent agents, and a Mac mini under a desk is not production
consume the accessibility tree and ARIA tags, and adopt WebMCP where sites publish it
plan authentication deliberately (scoped service accounts, agent-first signup flows, human-in-the-loop approval for sensitive actions) rather than handing agents passwords
feed observability — recordings, logs, network — back into the agent every run so it improves
and if browsing is not your core product, use a purpose-built browsing agent as a subagent instead of rebuilding one
data.name: Build browser agents as harness + infra, not model wait-states

guidelines: Start from a video/world model focused on humans rather than a bespoke avatar method — it's harder to train but gives emergent physics, movement, micro-expressions and emotions more cheaply
invest heavily in audio, since emotion and expression are driven by it and standard audiobook-trained encoders are too monotone

make the model real-time with three moves — a causal (past-only) attention mask (the future doesn't exist at inference), step distillation from ~30 denoising steps to 1, and a real solution to error accumulation (past-only generation compounds its own drift, fatal for hour-long streams)

and recognize that the model harness is where much of the value is — orchestrating streaming data across GPU and CPU so the video never stutters through interrupts, queues and buffering, especially for real-time
architecturally, expect to split an EQ layer (end-to-end video+audio with internal state) from a separate IQ model for reasoning and tool use
data.name: Build real-time avatars on a human-focused world model

guidelines: Treat real-time as a medium change, not a speedup — the value is the feedback loop that makes video programmable (addressable, changeable mid-stream), so design for interaction rather than better one-shot generation
know the three model classes and that combining them (infinite interactive video + controllable worlds + live avatars) is where new experiences emerge

build real-time infrastructure, not batch — stream pixels server-to-client, treat every generation as a live session with memory (solving the forgetting problem is core, since world models lose coherence when the view changes), and place GPUs globally for sub-100ms latency or the medium breaks
look beyond entertainment to robotics training-data generation (simulate any environment for infinite data) and education
and accept that consistency evaluation is unsolved — fidelity is pixels but coherence is human judgment today, so don't over-claim measurable quality
data.name: Build for real-time interactive video as a new medium

guidelines: Assume a deterministic benchmark is gameable — a <1MB replay of recorded successful trajectories will match your frontier model, and pass@k on a static environment is literally that replay's success rate, so treat a high pass@k as unproven until you check for replay

design environments to the PRISM principles — multifactorial variation (data, appearance, initial state), per-combination validity verification, sandboxing, verifier support, and realistic reproduction — since no existing benchmark satisfies all of them

generate variation with coding agents but verify every combination, because volume of software is not the same as a valid environment — use a compiler-like pipeline of parameterized template + verifier + mock data that assembles configs and rejects broken ones
measure model robustness across variation axes (starting screen, theme, data profile), not just one configuration, because frontier models often lose much of their performance under variation

and report coverage, not interval width — rollout-only confidence intervals give ~20% coverage while looking tight, so use a hierarchical method that respects benchmark structure, and when it says you can't confidently decide between two models, spend more on evaluation rather than making a costly wrong deployment call
data.name: Build CUA benchmarks a blind script can't beat

guidelines: Prototype the loop locally with your coding agent before automating it, then run the identical thing on a trigger

wire two trigger classes — periodic (e.g. every five minutes) and event-based (each error) — and start from traces, since AI systems already have traces at the core of the agent framework, with logs alongside
assemble the combination that lets the agent act (production traces/logs pulled by skills + the repo so the code path is legible + eval values already layered on the traces)
choose the pieces explicitly — harness (Claude Code), sandbox (own VPC sandbox, Anthropic managed agents, Daytona), skill set, driving prompt ("look for security issues")
track running agents as a fleet with viewable sessions and downloadable transcripts, and allow resuming a session locally to continue debugging by hand
close the loop by converting each confirmed issue into an evaluator or a dataset entry so the same failure is caught next time
data.name: Build the trace-to-PR loop, local first

guidelines: Require all three properties of every task — checkable by a function, durable across valid analysis paths (or correct work will be failed), and impossible to answer in one turn from memorized knowledge
when end-outcome grading is too sparse, decompose the analysis DAG and define ground truth at an intermediate node, taking the data to the state just before human interpretation
structure each eval as data node(s) + task prompt + grader config + deterministic grader
run two rounds of scientist cross-grading and expect it to expose defective tasks (unspecified choices, inherited arbitrary thresholds) rather than defective models
publish the human-verified subset
budget realistically for long-horizon tasks — a three-person week each — and don't trust choke-point rubrics for RL until they correlate numerically with the verifiable outcomes
data.name: Manufacture verifiability by choosing where to cut

guidelines: Treat a big data-access ask as infrastructure, not a feature — collection, transfer, storage, delivery at the reliability your consumer (AI training or agent retrieval) demands — and expect the first iteration to be wrong: clients buy your ability to adapt, so instrument for fast iteration (downloader → transcripts → subtitles → search → metadata was one product's real path)

for retrieval latency, don't just speed up the general scraper — scope it to what AI systems actually need (organic results, top stories) and cut heavy layout, because sub-second delivery is a capability gate that decides which products can exist, and it's won by many small cuts not a breakthrough

when scaling throughput, past a point adding servers doesn't help — you need an architecture, reliable central components, observability that stays truthful as telemetry becomes part of the load, and load tests using organic (real-usage-like) traffic, not just synthetic, accepting that the final test is production traffic

and design for constant change — targets, layouts, anti-bot detection and client needs all shift, so the durable product is the maintenance underneath, letting customers build intelligence on top while the messy upkeep stays with you
data.name: Build web-data infrastructure for an adapt-forever business

guidelines: Buy side: give agents a managed wallet (Coinbase or Stripe) through a payments service rather than raw keys
cap every payment session by amount and expiry
keep private keys in KMS so the agent never holds them
route 402 responses to the payment service, not the model
keep the payment path deterministic and separate from the agent loop because skills and inputs can be poisoned
discover paid endpoints through a gateway
turn on observability for every settlement. Sell side: detect and classify bots at the edge (type, verified signature, intent)
price by path, identity and intent with combinable rules
monetize over x402 at the CDN without touching origins
give verified partners their own rates and keep humans free where you choose
MCPify internal APIs behind the same gateway and meter them too
and measure with revenue-by-bot dashboards
data.name: Wallet under the agent, meter at the edge, keys in neither

guidelines: Evaluate hardware by what it will run in 6–18 months, not what it runs today (densing law: ~50% fewer parameters per capability every ~3.5 months)
Don't sell working GPUs — their capability grows as models densify (Osman keeps his 3090s for what they'll do in a year, not their resale price)
Prefer actively developed architectures (Blackwell / DGX Station) whose software stack keeps improving
Track "impact per parameter" — what capability ran on what footprint a year ago vs now — when deciding rent vs own. (Speaker's own caveat: not financial advice)
data.name: Size local-AI hardware against the densing curve, not today's models

guidelines: Give the accountable domain team — not engineering, not the model provider — ownership of the definition of good

vibes don't count. Turn each labeled scenario into concrete questions (did the expected observation fire, did the right category trigger, at the right point in the conversation, did the output evaluator catch the issue type) and gate releases on them. Count false positives and false negatives, plus category and timing, as first-class costs — in a care setting over-triggering is its own harm, so the aim is to shrink the margin rather than to pick a preferred failure direction. Do not pursue benchmark perfection: real ambiguity exists in edge cases, and chasing the number drifts focus away from the humans the benchmark protects — build benchmarks from real failure modes in real data instead. Where the domain has collective stakes, publish a clinically reviewed baseline set so other builders don't learn on live users
data.name: Calibrate the gate; don't maximize the benchmark

guidelines: Every hack that makes someone's life easier goes to production and stays there — you will support it in perpetuity, so treat "this is just temporary" as the most dangerous sentence in the job. Before shipping, answer four questions: will this generate a 2 a.m. call in six months
is this trade-off right for the product as a whole or only for this customer's pain point (small win now, negative compounding later)
who inherits it when I leave the site — the customer, another FDE, another institution
and what happens, and who is blamed, when it breaks. Decide explicitly whether each solution folds into the core offering or gets discarded quickly
a hack that wins goodwill but doesn't move product strategy is solutions-architect work, not FDE work
data.name: Ship fast, but build as if it runs for 18 months

guidelines: Decide what to point AI at yourself — it is the one decision it can't make, and it comes from being close to a real domain and a real customer
don't bet on broad "taste" (trainable) but on judgement about what hasn't happened yet and on relationships the model can't observe
state your claim in one sentence with the limit welded in (never "intelligent AI-native platform")
make the limit un-editable — visible in the product and printed next to every impressive number in launch copy so remixes keep the honest part
read-back test with an outsider (hand a README to an SRE who has never seen it and ask them to describe the product back) before scaling
fix organization distortion by reattaching the signal to the outcome like a founder, not by adding process
use AI aggressively for the converging work — formatting, drafting, algorithm optimization, cleanup — around a core it could not have generated
and remember the average is not free — you pay for it in tokens, infra and people
data.name: Define the signal yourself, protect it from distortion, automate everything else

guidelines: Model agents in a runtime that checkpoints state and can replay from code
start from real production runs, never synthetic
build cohorts that matter (most expensive, longest, riskiest)
replay one change across the cohort (model swap, mocked tool, degraded dependency), diff against the grounded baseline, judge on value delivered not cost alone
never ship off one or two replays
be selective about what you replay (cohort replay is expensive)
automate the loop — ideally an agent runs it — with a human in the loop at the end
data.name: Evaluate changes by replaying production, not synthesizing tests

guidelines: Decide deliberately where the boundary of your training stack sits
In-stack Q&A: full control of rollout code and chat format, single-turn only
Synthetic environment: push environment state out (tool specs, initial file system, sandbox), keep the orchestrator — you keep replayability, so GRPO still works, and you take on fidelity risk

Bring your own harness: keep only the completion endpoint and a request/response recorder — you get the deployment distribution exactly and give up replayability, parallel rollouts per prompt, and format guarantees, so plan for off-policy methods from the start rather than porting a GRPO recipe
If you own the harness, staying at the synthetic rung is usually right
if the customer owns it — especially if you cannot read its source — you are at the BYOH rung whether you planned for it or not
data.name: Pick the rung by what you can afford to lose

guidelines: If the agent lives inside a product: use TypeScript for agent loop, tools, backend, and UI (one language, one repo, one type system via Zod)
Tap NPM for auth/payments/UI/infra integrations
Expect coding-agent output quality in TS to keep improving with the flywheel
Keep Python for training, research, and model serving — don't split the app into FastAPI + React unless you must
data.name: Build application-layer agents in TypeScript, keep training in Python

guidelines: Four classes, drawn from what Harbor users actually build: (1) agents build your product — benchmark coding agents on your own internal codebase (RampBench pattern) so agent/model selection is an informed decision rather than a token-spend maximization

(2) agents use your product — assume a headless mode is coming, build an eval for how well agents operate your product, then iterate the product against it, since agent-usability compounds into agent usage
(3) agents power product features
(4) agents automate internal processes
One or more applies to every company
the instruction is to pick and start now
data.name: Pick your eval class from your business model

guidelines: Parse the document with Docling
hand the agent the markdown outline with per-section summaries as the entire retrieval index
loop (~5 iterations): pick the sections most relevant to the query, pull their full text from the structured document, judge whether they answer the question, iterate if not
works from a 20-section paper to a 418-section annual report
skip the chunker/embedding/vector-database stack entirely for single-corpus Q&A
data.name: Answer questions over big documents without a vector DB

guidelines: Ask what the goal of the task is, not whether a human happens to be present: if the goal is to please the person in the loop, today's models are excellent and getting better
if the goal is to remove them — to run in a server nobody watches until it becomes boring legacy software — an RLHF-trained model is structurally mismatched and will look right when it is wrong
Practical consequences: never put business-stakes decisions behind a preference-optimized model
assume a persistent gap between how good an output looks and how good it is
expect an agent that is improving at agentic work to simultaneously drift from what you asked (that is the two objectives trading off, not a prompt bug)
and treat the currently-standard mitigation — pushing all the costs onto the user rather than your business — as a symptom to be designed out, not a pattern to copy
data.name: Classify the task before you pick the model

guidelines: (1) Classify the profession's tasks on the three axes — asymmetry (can it be decomposed into checkable steps), veracity (is there consensus on what correct means), proliferation (does the world hand you fresh verified examples). (2) Apply the long-horizon bar labs actually use, and note vendors define it inconsistently: enforced step length, heterogeneous tool calls that aren't interchangeable, state transitions that genuinely constrain future actions, and mandatory failure recovery. (3) Inspect the raw data for the qualifying signals: sequential decisions taken against a single entity, an inferable expert action at each step, outcomes recorded by independent parties, and — economically — high-wage work that is actually available to capture. Plot the result on share-of-white-collar-work against task horizon: short horizons are addressable today, but the long-horizon tail is where the economic value and the data build-out live, and the frontier line moves rightward every time somebody builds a real-world data pipeline
data.name: Read which domain matures next, with a three-step checklist

guidelines: Seller side: solve a real problem the platform team can't rebuild in six weeks
price on value, never on the buyer's own gateway telemetry
show integrations on day one
let the buyer write success criteria
offer ZDR (and mean it) or CMEK that doesn't break the product
support BYO gateway and deployment into the buyer's cloud with a 90-day plan
ship SCIM-tied RBAC and every admin setting via API with audit logs and controlled rollouts
never default to read-write-all scopes or betas-on
hire a security person and have a breach plan and an architecture diagram before the pilot
keep a status page, real SLAs and a reachable support engineer

keep contract terms out of support pages and never hide data retention in a beta clause. Buyer side: start with the boring 60% — fix entitlements, governance and audit logging before agents 100× the problem
move integration up the stack
centralize knowledge so agents can be thin
and spin up a separate experimentation ecosystem when the legacy gap is too vast
data.name: Sell into — and prepare — a regulated enterprise

guidelines: Start in the CLI, not the editor
keep several terminals of agent runs in parallel
keep the editor for fine adjustments and as the control board
scale via /delegate (requires a proper GitHub repo) or assign-issues-to-agent from the GitHub UI
let sandboxed agents produce draft PRs and keep humans as the approval gate — review before merge, add more approval gates as needed
data.name: Run a CLI-first, delegate-to-PR workflow

guidelines: Take the highest-fidelity signal you have — daily customer contact — and route it back to product deliberately, not incidentally. For each challenge, ask whether it is common across the enterprise or unique to one user, and whether a workaround, hack or bug should become a feature. Always ask why the problem matters to the business as a whole and whether it can be communicated back in a way that improves things for every other customer

the goal is a de-risked roadmap. Flag engineering practices that need fixing with no ego attached — "we are all in the same boat". Treat every role as go-to-market: the target is customer success at all costs, and everybody owns it
data.name: Treat the field as the eval set and close the loop into the roadmap

guidelines: Patch validation ladder: original PoC stops working → test suite stays green → a fresh discovery agent re-attacks the patched code
feed that back to the patching agent (quality improves greatly)
human confirms before merge
record compensating controls in the scan config so the finding never resurfaces — start with open-source dependencies, interactively ("hands on the wheel"), before aiming for automation
data.name: Validate patches on a ladder, then encode what you learned

guidelines: Before acting on simulated results, measure the sim-to-real gap: compute your eval metrics on simulated data and on real production data and check the correlation
have domain experts review sampled simulated conversations and label whether the data is usable
run the check for greenfield agents too, not only mature ones where you have production data to compare against
once calibrated, change the release gate rather than adding a step: iterate against simulation and launch only the variant you are already happy with in sim, so the quarter's ten A/B tests become one
keep metrics honest in parallel — align judge classifiers to human judgment and keep improving them with automated prompt optimization
data.name: Earn the right to trust simulated evals

guidelines: Prompt-engineer one isolated variable per variant: numbered-message input vs raw JSON, few-shot examples, strict negative rules, chain-of-thought — here few-shot won (better length/accuracy, +200 ms) while explicit "don't" rules made the small model worse
Move structural checks into deterministic post-processing (ref-count validation against thread length, truncation for length)
Crack open raw eval outputs before trusting judge scores
Then keep regression evals running CI/CD-style so a prompt tweak or model upgrade can't silently blow up the feature ("how you keep your CTO from blowing away your agentic experience one morning")
data.name: Close the SLM-frontier gap in the harness, then guard it

guidelines: Log a flat end-to-end record from day one
declare one guardrail metric per component (recall for a router that must not pass bad inputs) and never ship below it
sample production on a fixed cadence to the same labelers under the same guidelines used for the golden set
diff agent output against those labels
route mismatches into a diagnoser that localizes the failing component rather than re-tuning everything
split the optimizer into reflect (denoise the mismatches, extract systemic issues) and synthesize (rewrite the config from that feedback)
gate every rewrite on a golden-set re-benchmark
version agents in a store so production picks up the new config and rollback is one step
keep observability on the guardrails of the loop itself
data.name: Build the tuning loop, not just the agent

guidelines: If a task has an exact answer, reach for code — cheaper, more reliable ("AI did not invent automation")
if it needs interpretation, judgment, or reasoning over messy input, give it to the agent
keep authority with humans — the human approves booking the tour
data.name: Assign work by actor strength

guidelines: Keep one pinned project (personal monorepo) as a git repo
store code outside it (AGENTS.md: "save code in /dev")
add front-matter to each project file linking its relevant Slack channels, and to each person file their emails/Slack/work addresses, so the agent reads the right context automatically
make the vault a git repo and git diff to review what the agent changed
optionally run automations that garden the vault
data.name: Run a personal monorepo memory vault

guidelines: Every derived figure that appears in no filing — gross margin, enterprise value, the EBITDA adjustment set, what counts as recurring — is calculated differently by every firm, so the firm's conventions must be codified into the processes that run, not inferred per query
record a chain of events for each number and each outcome so both can be replayed and rewound, the way an analyst's reasoning on a desk can be walked back

declare up front which data points the system is allowed to produce (structured filings, numerical data) and which it is never allowed to produce — if it would have to extract from prose or a raw table, it doesn't
then every consolidated statement can be shipped with each number tied to its individual source, and the work product itself becomes the proof
data.name: Codify the firm's conventions, then record the chain

guidelines: Put an agents.md at every level of the system explaining the workflow, where policy lives, supporting resources (skills, scripts, sub-agents), and how to keep memory up to date
the test: a fresh-context human or agent can orient and act without reverse-engineering prompts
if a harness fails when asked to update the system, treat that as a maintainability bug
data.name: Build for the fresh-context cold start

guidelines: Know who your raters are, what they like and why — then attach that profile to every datum, so the dataset expresses a multi-preference world rather than a contradictory one
Force the distribution deliberately: select experts across mediums and styles so coverage is a controlled variable, not an accident of recruiting

QC on measurable properties rather than vibes — score the specificity of an expert's reasoning as a proxy for signal richness, and tie each critique to the exact code component it refers to, because models can't reliably connect a rendered visual back to its source

Run human QA in two passes: screen the objective fundamentals (spec adherence, alignment), then run expert consensus and read the disagreements by attribute — divergence on objective attributes means bad data, divergence on aesthetics means you found a real preference boundary and should keep it
And prefer depth to volume: high-taste expert data beats large noisy datasets in these domains
data.name: Collect preference data that doesn't average itself away

guidelines: State the why and the desired outcome, not step-by-step instructions
Expect self-micromanagement ("don't tell Claude to improve itself — you'll get micromanagement") and pull the agent back to intent
The same doctrine improves delegation to humans
data.name: Prompt with commander's intent

guidelines: For role-playing systems: anchor primary documents in the context window at inference instead of fine-tuning them into weights
fix a temporal anchor (the specific life moment the persona speaks from — knowledge postdating it is out of bounds)
keep prompt, corpus, and temporal anchor as versioned repo artifacts (diffable, revertible)
keep a human curator with interpretive custody over what enters and what emerges
treat the model as the swappable voice, not the mind
data.name: Compose the encounter; don't train the persona

guidelines: Work backwards from the RL phase

Ensure the base model has exposure to the atomic skills it will need to compose — RL extrapolates from atoms it has seen, but it will not discover them for you — and make the RL environment difficult enough that extrapolation is required

Deliberately introduce novel-shaped data during supervised learning: shapes the model would not otherwise have seen, such as reasoning traces (which "don't really look like a ton of what humans output") and test-time-compute schemes, so the shape is not new at the moment RL starts
Expect the mix to look nothing like a knowledge corpus: code and STEM over general web text, with web text a supporting rather than dominant share
data.name: Build the base model as a prior for the RL you intend to run

guidelines: Treat every pipeline as the same six components — seeds, primary inputs, metadata, secondary inputs, a generator function (prompt template or tool-using agent), and supplementary functions (filters, validators) — then pick a point on the complexity axis per data class: cheap, seed-heavy, small-model pipelines for bulk (where output quality rides almost entirely on seed quality, so invest there), orchestrated multi-agent workflows only where the data justifies the cost. Four shapes cover most of it: rephrasing (break token repetition

ablate against the repeated-seed baseline), multi-stage decomposition (don't generate the novel — generate setting, characters, styles, plot and twists first, then the chapters), cross-domain porting (translate between modes — code to another language, math problems into code), and multi-turn loops (two agents in conversation, or a judge and an evolver alternating for k rounds). Governing rule of thumb: if a task is too hard for the generating model it loses both correctness and diversity — break it down and make each step simpler, which is what frees you from the ceiling of whatever the teacher model can do in one shot. Run it on infrastructure that makes this configurable: a queue of agents with per-agent prompt/parameters/model and entry, exit and frequency rules, orchestrators between agents to impose hierarchy, rewrite the next agent's instructions and route or skip agents, and a supervisor with a global view policing the orchestrator
data.name: Compose synthetic pipelines from six parts and four shapes

guidelines: SFT the small model from a larger teacher first, then on-policy RL with: retrieval reward = ranking metric (NDCG on the final list) + LLM retrieval judge over rubrics (results relevant to query? all chunks relevant? ranking plausible?), and trajectory reward = LLM judge over the process (is each query a natural sentence? is exploration sufficient — neither too much nor too little? is the run efficient?) — rewarding the search behavior, not just the end answer
data.name: Train small search agents with a two-part reward

guidelines: Feed the loop the four primitives first: skills as your organization's (and your customers') secret recipes so agents follow the correct workflow rather than improvising one
MCP so the agent reaches whatever third-party system holds the data — logging, auth gateway, client systems
sub-agents in parallel worktrees
and minimal UX

then compound it: after each one-to-two-day run of five or six tickets, have the agent enumerate the bottlenecks in the process it just ran, keep the list, and remove one per day — after about a month a single sentence drives the whole pipeline
add goals plus loops for unattended runs you can steer from a phone, and background "dreaming" that compacts recurring customer-session patterns into data the system uses to upgrade itself
keep the verifier: in a regulated domain the reviewer and the signer must be human, so design the loop so that constraint costs you latency at the boundary and nothing in the middle
data.name: Make the loop audit itself, daily

guidelines: Attach a confidence score to every agentic decision
require multi-source evidence concurrence before auto-proceeding
return contradictory facts alongside supporting ones
route only low-confidence/contradictory cases to humans
keep every rule configurable for override
add a self-healing loop for fragile integrations
data.name: Gate no-touch automation on confidence + corroboration

guidelines: Design the rules of play: decide enable vs govern (how much guardrail), reward cohering toward the goal vs cost falling outside the container, and tune the coupling rate (dial interaction up or dampen it)

then sense and respond to the emergent harness rather than hard-editing it. Guard the known failure modes: inject genuine selection pressure (emergence settles into attractors that feel stable but aren't optimal — without pressure you get drift), preserve agent diversity (same-training-data monoculture kills the variance emergence feeds on), and accept the costs — legibility collapse and no ahead-of-runtime predictability
data.name: Engineer constraints and pressure, not outcomes

guidelines: Write every task from scratch rather than scraping closed PRs, and recruit the authors from among the repo's own core contributors and maintainers so the task is realistic as both a prompt and a mergeable PR

run the authoring as a competitive platform per domain so supply scales. Spread coverage: keep the median tasks-per-repository near 1 (91 repos for 113 tasks) instead of thousands of tasks from ~40 repos, gate repos on activity and popularity (>500 stars) plus SME validation, and span multiple languages. Then strip the environment: separate the verifier runtime from the agent runtime, trim every git ref and commit except the base commit, and standardize test-report format
data.name: Author tasks instead of mining them

guidelines: Longer context ≠ better — every irrelevant file/web result/error drags attention
keep pre-conversation load (system prompt + tools + MCPs) under ~40% of the window or you start in the dumb zone
prefer progressive disclosure over dumping tool definitions and documents
data.name: Treat context as a budget with a 40% ceiling

guidelines: Embed live, mandatory, frequently-updated data sources (GitHub, CRM, Tableau/dbt semantic layers) rather than hand-maintained .md files
log every correction event ("this definition is wrong/updated")
evaluate continuously — human-annotated suite or automated regression against recent Q&A — and update context on a cadence
data.name: Run a context lifecycle, not static context

guidelines: Don't hand the agent the Datadog (etc.) token: a credential-management proxy injects the real secret on the fly when the agent calls the API, so the credential is usable by but never readable from the agent
provision Claude its own identity/credentials rather than acting as the user, which also gives clean audit trails
data.name: Make credentials usable but not accessible to agents

guidelines: Layer 1 — entity-correlation graph across payroll/tax/procurement/finance ("what is connected?"). Layer 2 — adaptive probabilistic risk scoring combining anomaly strength, source reliability, and historical patterns into a confidence-based score ("what is genuinely risky?"), continuously retrained on audit outcomes. Layer 3 — cross-jurisdictional normalization of currencies, tax rules, reporting periods, classification schemes ("how should risk be interpreted here?"). Deployment: integrate with existing ERP/payroll/procurement/tax platforms
configure per jurisdiction
align outputs with the audit workflow so investigators work a prioritized risk-scored queue instead of routine document review
validate scalability to millions of records
data.name: Build compliance AI as three layers over connected data

guidelines: Once the architecture is locked, put the work into data curation, because it determines model quality more than any other choice

decide deliberately what "good" means — optimizing standard aesthetic/quality scores mode-collapses toward the boring average, so if you want stylistic diversity you must *not* cut unconventional aesthetics (low-res, CRT, etc.)
dedup in stages (cheap pHash/MD5 first, then embedding-based SSCD/SigLip for near-duplicates)
scale filtering by distilling a large VLM's judgement into a cheap SigLip-sized classifier you can run over a billion images, and use SAE unsupervised tagging for oversample/filter features
remove AI-generated images despite the shortcut they offer, because synthetic data is sticky and collapses your model toward frontier aesthetics you can't undo
borrow the LLM post-training recipe (pre/mid-train, SFT, preference optimization, GRPO with reward servers, a prompt-expander, multi-expert distillation) to reuse kernels and literature
and check captioner failure modes, since a captioner that consistently omits a fact (e.g. "framed on a white wall") biases every generation
data.name: Curate data as the real lever for image models

guidelines: Decompose curation into stages (source, mix, filter, generate, filter) and settle each stage with an ablation rather than intuition
use LLMs to score question quality and hardness during filtering
sample multiple answers per question instead of buying more questions (16x on one question beat 16x the questions — the diversity of reasoning traces is what fine-tuning consumes)
test teacher models empirically, because bigger is not reliably a better teacher
don't assume answer filtering, synthetic question rewriting or task augmentation help — all three underdelivered
publish/keep the recipe and validate it by showing metrics scale with dataset size before spending on scale
apply the identical method to agent trajectories and environments
data.name: Stage it, ablate it, then prove the scaling curve

guidelines: Every expensive dataset gets an MD record: LLM-enriched description, session context (why it was built), storage dependency, data preview, stats, and — most important — the generating source code
source data + code + warehouse result = lineage, so teammates' agents reuse results instead of paying double/triple recompute
data.name: Share computed datasets as an agent-readable knowledge base

guidelines: Partner before launch and take the architecture details early (attention scheme, MoE layout, quantization)
triage against your existing kernels — reuse, modify, or write from scratch
make quality, not throughput, the day-zero bar so users get the model the lab intended
keep a standing optimization backlog (KV cache, attention kernels, quantization) and burn it down weekly so the same weights get faster at day 7 and day 14
carry lessons across sparse-attention families rather than restarting per model
leave no stone unturned — "if someone tells you you can't do the thousand-and-first thing, try harder"
data.name: Ramp a new open model from day zero

guidelines: Use aggregator APIs and tool calls wherever they exist — clicking buttons on flights.google.com when aggregators return JSON is theater

reserve computer use for the long tail, and audit whether your target sites are head or tail before choosing an architecture (does the institution behind the page have the capacity to ever publish an interface?)
do not trust initially-loaded HTML as the page — content arrives asynchronously and visible states are often rendered consequences with no textual representation, so verify through pixels
prefer a model that can both click and write code, using the screenshot as the success check for either path
expect per-site scaffolds not to transfer, and treat rising accuracy plus falling latency and cost — not protocol adoption — as the trend line that decides when to move a workflow onto agents
and parallelize across cloud browser instances for workloads no human could span
data.name: Decide when a task needs computer use rather than an API

guidelines: Cost tech debt like financial debt against the ROI it bought (features, customers) — complexity can outrun the ROI. Weigh that refactoring later gets exponentially easier (better models, tool calling, sandboxes, monitoring), but that AI-native velocity without guardrails recreates legacy conditions (much code, low quality, no one understands it) — so guardrails are mandatory whether you refactor fully, partially, or not at all

isolating codebase layers is a legitimate middle path. If you commit: consolidate to a monorepo first (agent E2E testing/verification/deployment and sandbox economics favor it), reach parity, then build features
use human PR review early as deliberate context-building for the new repo

adopt lifecycle primitives (plan mode, review skills) as they mature. Measure the outcome in business terms — pipeline time, cost, max file size, feature latency, parity time, post-parity commit velocity, contributor spread — and in whether developers *want* to work in the codebase
data.name: Decide refactors on business value under exponential agent progress

guidelines: For each agent action ask whether the human authorized it, whether it is allowed right now in this scope, and whether you can prove it later
place the action by stakes and by whether the counterparties share a trust boundary
low stakes inside your own boundary — OAuth consent, allow/deny/ask permissions, system logs, reversibility
money inside a closed ecosystem — a credential vault, OAuth-scoped access, a mandate with amount, time and merchant limits, transaction logs
money among strangers — verifiable intents and AP2-style layered mandates the user signs, so each party verifies its slice
make time-bound, amount-bound, merchant-bound authorizations the default
build asynchronous human confirmation (approval tokens) into checkout rather than synchronous approval
and reuse the model for any hard-to-reverse action
data.name: Three questions, two axes, three rows

guidelines: Before fine-tuning, test each reason against a context-based rebuild: accuracy (a skills/context system on a frontier model may beat it — it did here)
cost (compare total cost including the retrain cycle, not per-message API cost)
latency (small-model gains are marginal in practice)
narrow structured task (even the textbook case calcified)
vendor control (fine-tunes lock you to one provider's formats and versions — context gives the portability)
keep fine-tuning for privacy/data-control or offline constraints, and then only if it still beats the tax

if you have fine-tuned, expect the calcification tax — week-long whack-a-mole, a frozen model, a frozen architecture — and plan the migration to skills, tools and resources with a curated production validation set and markdown-file deploys so fixes take an hour, not a week
data.name: Cross off your reasons, then beat the tax

guidelines: The six: (1) fund R&D, (2) fund growth, (3) founder ego, (4) reward/liquidity for employees, (5) strategic partnership, (6) M&A. Be honest about which one applies — ego raises are "very dangerous… you're diluting all of your employees" and pricing future hires' upside for a status game. Bootstrapping discipline as default (revenue > bills before salaries)
offer investors the shutdown-and-return option if conviction is unproven
raise #4 deliberately so employees don't wait a decade for an IPO to see upside
data.name: Name which of the six reasons you're raising for

guidelines: Spot the distinct jobs hiding in one prompt and rehome each: reusable process → agent skill (write once, load in every market)
fixed output format → schema
exact computation → plain boring script
meaty research subtask → sub-agent. Don't abstract instructions local to one workflow — modularity sometimes costs more than it saves
data.name: Decompose the blob prompt by responsibility

guidelines: Think in three layers and keep their abstractions separate
make state durable and external — a 3-hour run cannot hold state in memory or on disk
never use sandboxes for durability (sandbox = hands, execution = brain
execution gives the sandbox its context, sequence, durability)
demand resumability (retry/wait/continue from a failed step 38, not from the beginning)
use flexible invocation primitives (cron, events, APIs, human-in-the-loop, sync/async/delayed, sub-agents) so harness logic doesn't absorb queues, workers, polling, backoff
require full-session traces from trigger through the whole stack, not just LLM/tool calls
data.name: Decouple execution, context, and compute

guidelines: Run inference, trainer, and orchestrator as separate processes that only consume from each other (no shared GPUs)
environments as engines that send requests/batches over APIs
scaling concerns then decouple (N environments, M inference replicas, sandboxes or none) and the same environments double as standalone evals — avoid folding training+inference into one logical stack
data.name: Pull the RL stack apart into client-server pieces

guidelines: Assume any proxy reward is undefined at its boundaries and will be exploited
don't rely on instructing the model not to hack, and don't assume in-rollout judges will catch it

instead replay trajectories with multiple models and look for agreement on what went wrong, distill the agreement into rubric questions that audit future rollouts cheaply, keep a growing corpus of observed hacks so you learn the shape of your own failure modes, run adversarial prompt optimization as red-teaming to find backdoors, and log behavioural metrics during training (judge questions about tool-call patterns) — then do small RL runs as part of environment design, because some hacks only appear once you train
data.name: Audit in hindsight, and validate by training

guidelines: Define exactly what done means per task, in detail
separate verifier from author — ideally a different model (code with Claude, verify with Codex)
require evidence, and give agents the tools to produce it (custom browser harness, screenshots, hooks/tooling to click through and try the work themselves)
establish a clear chain of custody — every agent knows who receives the work next
set explicit reviewers and approvers so completion triggers review
use goal-holding watchdogs to keep work moving within bounds
data.name: Define done for agent work (the "100× checklist")

guidelines: Treat vocabulary as the first deliverable. Inventory which terms are overloaded — the same entity called customers, clients, billing entities and org IDs by four teams

DAU meaning quality-weighted actives to product and raw logins to infosec. Locate the integration points between systems (Snowflake to Databricks, platform to Tableau, model provider to ERP) and the translation layers where one term becomes another. Identify the system boundaries: which systems of record will never be swapped out. Listen to the words people use when describing failures, and interrogate the loose ones ("my agent keeps failing" — is an agent a prompt, a series of steps?). Then canonicalize: pick the terms, encode them in the platform as entities and operations, and get customers answering questions in your vocabulary — that is what makes you the foundation later tools are built on
data.name: Map the nouns and verbs before you map the data

guidelines: Write the questions users will ask from the business process before building, score honestly, and ship fewer answers at higher accuracy
pilot with volunteers, beta with 10% until data requests concentrate and weekly retention holds above ~70%, then GA
budget months of change management — demos, adoption dashboards, manager comparisons, executive sponsorship — because activation, not technology, is where internal AI fails
plan the journey past talk-to-data into workflow automation, team-built skills and apps, and personalization, and expect the wow factor to collapse within months
launch with today's stack and accept 30–40% of every sprint as re-architecting
classify every question with LLMs and use the logs for feature gaps, quality issues, enablement generation and cross-team matchmaking
data.name: Quality first, phase the launch, drive activation, keep raising the bar, mine the logs

guidelines: Train two smaller dense models on curated data while simulating token scarcity so they sit on the same scaling curve as the large run
the line through them predicts a model trained with 50x more compute
Use it to discover that the hero run does not land where you want before you pay for it — the derisking costs 50-100x less than the run it protects
data.name: Predict the hero run from two small curated runs

guidelines: Assume fuzzy intent and build a working state from conversation history, personal context, hard constraints and image-inferred soft constraints with confidence scores, refreshing real-time variables such as inventory
find the intent gap and ask only about the unknown with the largest information gain, never over-asking
bridge each constraint to the merchant ontology as you go and choose the elicitation format per constraint — visual preference boards for subjective ones — while reading hovers and clicks
do comparisons and trade-offs in the background
pick the response format for the query (summary, trade-off table, visual board) so the answer is findable and actionable

put auto-raters on every stage (retention, calibration, counterfactual sensitivity, blockers, over-asking, question utility, elicitation efficiency with a user simulator, turn efficiency, format accuracy, data fidelity, actionability) and let them evolve with the system
keep response formatting on the agent side across merchants
and expect users to keep discovery for themselves and delegate comparison and negotiation
data.name: Accept vibes, show and ask, shape the answer, grade the loop

guidelines: Do not reach for RAG by default — neither leading assistant chunks-and-embeds conversations, and the architecture both converged on is a running profile synthesized in the background plus tools to search past conversations on demand
keep memory synthesis asynchronous so the user is never made responsible for curating memories while trying to have a conversation, which was the flaw that sank the first-generation fact list

budget memory explicitly as compute, trading update frequency against profile length, since the profile is injected into every conversation and its length is a per-conversation tax while its freshness is an update-cost tax — the two leading vendors sit at opposite corners of that trade-off and both are defensible
decide deliberately how dense the writing is, since keyword-cluster profiles pack more per token and lean on the model's inference while prose profiles are more legible to users
make the profile visible and editable, and treat an edit as triggering a resynthesis rather than a patch
design for staleness from the start, because facts true when written stop being true and the corpus of failures here is mostly stale-fact failures
build memory in-house alongside the product rather than outsourcing it, because the converged part is easy and the divergent part is product-specific

and invest in context acquisition and conflict detection — reason over the sources the user has already connected, and make the system notice and try to resolve contradictions rather than storing both
data.name: Design memory as a compute budget, and build it in-house

guidelines: Package the vulnerable application inside a container so runs are reproducible (the same binary behaves differently across Linux versions)
verify before shipping that at least one flaw exists and reproduces — from your own crash or a reproduced bug report
expose a small MCP surface: setup (returns the problem definition), sandboxed read/write tool calls inside the container, and the grading oracle at the end
always ask the model to exploit, never merely to report — the exploit input is the witness that separates a real finding from a hallucination
grade deterministically at every rung
keep an orchestrator between the model and the gym
data.name: Build a cybersecurity RL environment

guidelines: Design for retrieval first — the hard part is finding the right data (e.g. the group of traces belonging to one session)
materialize it into the repo as files, accepting large ones (10 MB temp files in the repo are normal) because "these harnesses are magical with files"
pick the file format deliberately so the harness parses it cheaply

decompose into composable skills that mirror real tool affordances (Pyroscope memory-issue skills, facet use, cohort-by-customer to isolate one customer's failures) so the agent can chain steps rather than call one monolithic query
expose eval results as trace-attached data with skills that fetch aggregate eval values across traces, giving the agent pre-processed assessment on top of raw telemetry
data.name: Design observability skills for a coding agent, not a dashboard

guidelines: State in guidelines that the AI signal is preliminary and the human is the final decision-maker
require independent evidence before upholding a flag
split compound CTAs into "was the detection correct?" and "is this a violation?"
match friction to stakes — deliberate review gates and speed bumps where stakes are high, seamless frictionless flow where oversight is low
prefer structured inputs/outputs (inline markup like the writing-tutor UI, forms, tables) over walls of text
make agents plan, ask good questions, and ship reviewable increments like a good junior developer
data.name: Design human-AI review for discernment, not approval

guidelines: Don't chain independent subtasks to inflate duration
make early decisions constrain later ones so a bad early query cascades (sequential complexity) rather than fanning out (parallelizable complexity)
widen tool coordination — logs, CI/CD, cloud consoles, databases — so information has to move across dependencies
introduce deliberate ambiguity in the opening instructions and artifacts to test exploration, and accept the grading cost that comes with it
check coverage across the domain's real subareas (credit/debt/risk, not just spreadsheet formatting) before claiming domain coverage
screen for learnability — reward density, task distribution, data quality — before spending training compute
data.name: Build state coupling, not length

guidelines: Snapshot only diffs (never full gigabytes per turn)
make the snapshot API cheap enough to call constantly — return before upload finishes
restore = create-from-snapshot, must be as fast as create
explicit save: CoW zero-copy layer over a base image + FIEMAP changed-extent bundling
always-on save: NBD block device over a tiered in-cluster cache writing back to object storage (avoid NFS — not performant, not POSIX-enough for models trained on POSIX)
data.name: Design sandbox persistence as incremental block-level snapshotting

guidelines: Watch for the signature: high shipping velocity + low adoption
logins/trials without **re-use** (track frequency of a specific activity, not time-on-site)
"the demo is the deliverable" (demos are fast and pretty — production use is the bar)
a PRD with no real user testers. Fix the measurements: replace "features shipped last quarter" with "features used more than twice"
move subject-matter experts into the decision-making about what gets built (they know what worked before) without forcing everyone to become a PM
data.name: Audit for building-the-wrong-thing anti-patterns

guidelines: Treat data quality and training-codebase correctness as one problem, not two — if you've got data that sucks you can't train a good model

if you've got a training code base that sucks, you also can't. Then find invariants you can actually check and enforce them: under distributed data parallel every replica must hold identical weights, so hash the weights per replica, compare periodically, and crash the run on any mismatch rather than letting it continue — that is what surfaces silent data corruption from a single bad GPU. Watch gradient norms next to the loss, not the loss alone: a run that flattens with a rising gradient norm is a numerics story, and the specific one to check is accumulation precision at the unembedding — activations grow during training, BF16 accumulation under tensor parallelism eventually runs out of precision, and the fix is to move that accumulation to FP32 and resume from the last good checkpoint. Audit third-party kernels the same way: FP8 GEMM kernels produced illegal memory accesses, NaN gradients, and a silent ~0.5% random-value gradient corruption. Know your blind spot — real runs have no replicas sharing both weights and data, so forward/backward equivalence and kernel race conditions escape the hash check entirely
build a redundant dry-run checker to cover it
data.name: Assume the training stack is lying to you, and instrument invariants

guidelines: Async scan on file write/modify (CLI, not MCP — no token cost)
Buffer newly-introduced issues to a temp file
Gate at session-stop
Surface only NEW issues to context
Fix-and-validate loop only when needed
data.name: Wire deterministic security hooks into the agent lifecycle

guidelines: Use hierarchical URIs as node IDs so any subtree is scopable by prefix filter (search post-filtered by URI "starts with")
keep the relationship vocabulary tiny (has, links-to) — naming granularity trades query precision against context-window manageability
make loads idempotent so full rebuild is always safe
pair with Lucene full-text + "semantic expansion" (model rewrites the query with synonyms from world knowledge) instead of vendor-locked vector wiring
document/link naming quality is load-bearing for traversal — add LLM assistance at ingest only when structure or link labels are poor
data.name: Deterministic document graphs before LLM extraction

guidelines: Prefer golden-artifact black-box comparisons (same inputs → same outputs) for attribution
keep the judge only where determinism is impossible
read traces before blaming the model — prompt examples, tool failures, and infra bugs masquerade as reasoning failures
domain-knowledge prompt sections are portable across tool architectures and work by focusing attention ("pigeonholing"), not teaching the model new facts
data.name: Evaluate deterministically; treat LLM-as-judge as the fallback

guidelines: If a Python function can do it (current date, product info, calculations), don't spend an LLM call — looping 3–4 agents on local models adds 20–30s and users leave

functions are fully controlled, hallucination-free, and unit-testable. Put guardrails before the model: intent regex + term dictionaries + an LLM classifier reject prompt injection and out-of-scope/medical queries pre-LLM with canned escalation responses. Keep the system prompt tiny by encoding do's/don'ts in code. Instrument everything with local telemetry (Langfuse): per-conversation traces, retrieved chunks, latency, model used, cost estimates, session/user tracking — plus a consent gate on the chat widget
data.name: Replace agents with functions; block before the LLM

guidelines: Ask Fable to log every unknown it hits while running (implementation notes with context on why it deviated) so you can see where map diverged from territory
afterwards have it quiz you on what happened so you can genuinely represent the work at PR/merge time — the core "stay in the loop" practice for long-leash models
data.name: Log deviations mid-run, get quizzed after

guidelines: Crystallize the value proposition around a painful problem and validate it with paying customers
understand your shelf space in the developer's life
derive channels from that shelf space and become the authority on the problem
friend the ecosystem and cross-pollinate
know your foes so you can differentiate
distribute early — sometimes before the product is ready
triage with the PMF compass: product signal > revenue → work distribution
revenue > signal → work product
equal → full speed
data.name: Lay the devtools GTM foundation (six hygiene steps + compass triage)

guidelines: (1) Legibility: when product people / software engineers / AI engineers join a research initiative, is it obvious where to concentrate and which tasks to pluck off? If ambiguous, fix the RPT process. (2) Repo: is it clear which bucket new code goes in, with templates and patterns to mimic — or are you fighting old abstractions every time (you've outgrown the architecture)? (3) Decomposition: can you consistently estimate timelines and name the right SME reviewers? Failures here usually point upstream to (1) or (2)
data.name: Diagnose the research-to-production pipeline with three questions

guidelines: Don't start at the AI coworker — climb copilot → synchronous → asynchronous → long-running, earning each rung by proving value and walking the business up with you
for services work, represent knowledge work as code so coding agents can do it, find how to parallelize serial work, and choose form factors per industry

have agents collaborate with employees on real work and capture the traces (tool calls, hiccups, the diff between AI output and what was submitted) as ground-truth evals that become weekly regression tests, and post-train on your out-of-distribution business data
customize per company, per user and per client
treat continual learning and enablement as one loop owned together
embed products where people already work (Excel, ERP, 3D tools, Outlook) to keep the enablement energy low
and show up in person — lunch-and-learns, their conferences, one-on-ones — because co-design doesn't happen over Zoom or support tickets
data.name: Earn the rungs, own the traces, touch grass

guidelines: Don't put a data-carrying proxy in the path (not scalable — it moves all the traffic)
use a directory that only matches intent ↔ capabilities and logs per provider

ship the protocol as three layers — an agent plugin (server-side: verify agent, issue grants, enforce constraints), an SDK (mints keys, assigns agent identity, exposes an MCP so hosts like Claude/Cursor connect), and the directory
constrain the agent so its only path to external services is through the protocol
data.name: Prefer a directory over a proxy for agent capability routing

guidelines: Separate the parts of a training loop that need one fast fabric from the parts that only look like they do — keep backpropagation and its collectives in a single RDMA-connected cluster, and treat the rollout fleet as serving jobs that can live anywhere because nothing all-reduces between them

define the movable unit as a serving island (one coherent endpoint or local group serving one policy version) rather than a process, so local parallelism and prefill/decode disaggregation stay an implementation detail inside it
make the cross-seam contract as thin as possible — policy version in, trajectories and metadata out

stop synchronizing full checkpoints and ship a lossless bitwise patch over the served low-precision view instead, so the engine reconstructs the exact version rather than an approximation and no additive drift accumulates
publish immutable, named weight versions to a shared board and make requests state both the target version and the acceptable set, returning the served version in the response
put a sidecar in front of unmodified engines to proxy, catch up, or answer *not ready*, so an out-of-date node degrades to unavailable rather than to silently wrong
and materialize artifacts in a standard layout (Hugging Face safetensors) so any engine, parallelism strategy, serving dtype or GPU generation can join the pool
data.name: Disaggregate RL rollouts from the trainer

guidelines: Run the agent in monitor mode on production data, multiple runs per case
Select for review the cases whose verdicts disagree across runs/models (not low-confidence ones — LLM confidence is unreliable)
Have humans clarify only that subset: fix the label or add the disambiguating feature
Feed both back. Small labeling effort, high return — and you're gathering customer-preference adaptation for free
data.name: Use disagreement-driven active learning as agent quality control

guidelines: Run an ensemble of large general models over your raw data with LLM-as-judge consensus to auto-label a specialized dataset

distill to a small task-specific model — and when your class list is fixed, drop the expensive general components (e.g., swap SAM 3's autoencoder for a DETR-class detector) instead of fine-tuning the big model and losing what made it good (open-vocabulary)
deploy the small model on-device/real-time
keep the general model for data prep and curation only
prefer models whose data/weights/recipes are open (Nemotron) so customization is safe and legal
data.name: Use frontier models to bootstrap specialized local models, not to serve production

guidelines: Dogfood daily and fix your own product rather than route around it
roll out to the whole company + brutally honest early customers first
hold features to an explicit internal bar of active users and retention before public ship — unpolished features churn and thereby self-block
keep behavioral evals (not just capability evals) for how the product feels, fed by ranked user complaints
data.name: Gate launches on internal usage, not roadmap

guidelines: Budget roughly 1% of the pre-training token count (100B tokens here)

Make the majority of the mix representative of the pre-training distribution and only a minority domain-specific — this is what prevents catastrophic forgetting, and done right the general capabilities rise alongside the domain ones

Then re-run your existing post-training harness on the mid-trained checkpoint rather than on the stock instruction-tuned model: expect roughly 2-3x the post-training delta from unchanged post-training data, because the initial policy is more accurate
data.name: Mid-train for a domain without losing the general model

guidelines: Split the tool layer into three kinds: plain functions
prompts-as-tools (a tool call that invokes a different model, e.g. an image model like Nano Banana while GLM 5.2 runs the loop)
and full sub-agents-as-tools (recursive). Add hooks that inject synthetic messages/tool-calls (e.g. current time — LLMs don't know it) and fire side effects
agent rules (turn/step caps, tool-call validation requirements)

and bake in a sandboxed per-agent filesystem plus sandboxed code execution as primitives — the big labs already learned chat needs a filesystem. Keep each agent's context minimal and delegate across agents in plain English
data.name: Anatomy of an ideal domain agent

guidelines: Constrain hallucination with a hard legality tool (never let the model reason about illegal moves)
give it an interactive domain sandbox (board with play/undo/variations) rather than static pre-computed analysis
expose engine evaluation on demand, not as the only truth
add a candidate-saliency tool (checks/captures/threats) so coverage includes plausible-but-bad moves a human would consider
mix in human-move models (Maia-style, rating-conditioned) and web history to target the audience's level
let the agent drive presentation (square highlights, arrows, brilliancy labels, excitement tags in ElevenLabs V3 TTS)
don't optimize cost early — err toward too-good analysis and tolerate redundant tool calls
data.name: Build an explainer agent for an engine-solved domain

guidelines: Coding agents excel because compiler/linter/tests close the loop

for other domains build the equivalent — Witan built a formula engine (recalculation) and a rendering engine (range → image with layout/formatting) as the source of truth the agent must verify against
fidelity must be near-complete or results degrade below baseline
CSV/TSV range views and rendered-image views earn their keep as complementary methods inside the loop (they failed as standalone representations, as did SQL and XML)
data.name: Build the feedback loop your domain lacks

guidelines: Distinguish anomaly (one-off; handle per criticality) from drift (baseline shift; rebaseline)
Then classify: structural (step added/removed — e.g., the coffee shop adding a membership question) → fold the new step into baselines and alerts
scale/volume → scale instances out or make calls asynchronous
covariate (traffic mix changed, system fine) → maintain segmented baselines or consciously raise the average-time baseline
behavioral (same request, new behavior) → consider rollback
Once classified, risk-assess the automated fix and canary it: 5–10% of nodes → monitor and verify → 100%
keep an admin confirmation before classification-triggered automation
data.name: Classify drift before acting

guidelines: Give the agent a CLI driving Chrome through CDP, not an MCP server, so sequences are programmed once and replayed without a model in the loop — capability is comparable but reuse, speed and token cost favor the CLI heavily
work through the digital senses — read the page via DOM, accessibility tree, or screenshot
sense state via network, console, logs
operate via clicks, keystrokes, navigation — and only learn the small CDP subset you need rather than all 57 domains
run a sense–act–verify loop, always verifying through a *different* channel than the one you acted on

climb the ladder only as high as the page forces — try an exposed API or synthetic JS click first (free and instant), escalate to a trusted CDP input-domain click when synthetic clicks are silently dropped (Chrome's trusted/untrusted stamp is why), and only reach real mouse paths with jitter, overshoot and vision when a page actively hunts bots
for timed or high-frequency challenges keep the loop in deterministic code and call a vision model only for the single perception step, because a model round-tripped per action burns the clock
and once something works, write the path down as code and/or an agent skill so you solve it once and reuse it forever
finally, run only against infrastructure and accounts you own
data.name: Drive a browser like a human, deterministically

guidelines: Collect breadcrumbs from everywhere the user works (boards, email, Slack, calendar, meeting transcripts)
Slow engine: mine weeks of activity for persona, routines, collaborators, goals
distill into a durable profile
reinforce it every time it holds
Fast engine: recompute live signals (overdue, suddenly urgent, active collaborators) over a short recent window, updated frequently
Precompute both offline
at serve time recompute only a thin slice and verify part of the context against live data, falling back to last-verified
Isolate sources so a bad feed can't break the rest
make adding a source cheap and purely additive
data.name: Build agent context as two engines on different clocks

guidelines: Ground in an existing standard (WCAG 2.2 pillars; adopt WCAG 3.0's graded scoring)
expose dials (input tolerance, step granularity) instead of a static easy-mode
use on-device vision (eye-gaze), tap-jitter, and focus-path monitoring to sense real-time friction
act, don't just watch — resize controls, inject exit routes from keyboard/focus traps, allow handwriting recognition

groundwork still needed: sub-16 ms decisions, game-outcome prediction before applying a change, long-term per-user memory, a shared game-state language across games, and faster chips paired with honest benchmarks
data.name: Build accessibility as a live, agent-tuned scale

guidelines: Cite sources (tooltips for quotes, links for external, side panels for research work)
show agentic action plans and get approval before execution (with always-allow settings for repeat flows)
label AI-generated content (disclaimer, watermark, asterisk) instead of letting users feel it was snuck in
indicate which parts of output need manual verification
stream output and have the model think out loud so users can assess mid-generation and pinpoint where things went wrong
data.name: Earn trust through verifiability and honesty

guidelines: Start with human review of everything + automated review on every PR
measure per-file-category whether automation catches 100% of issues and remove humans only there
keep code owners on critical cores
on every incident, update the reviewer to catch that class and add the offending PRs to a review eval set so it never regresses
expect ~6 months of investment, not an overnight switch
data.name: Earn your way out of human code review

guidelines: Don't force a persona onto a rating scale — surveys are a task format LLMs aren't practiced at, and the constraint flattens exactly the variance you were trying to measure
Ask for free text ("I'm somewhat interested

if it works well and isn't too expensive I might try it"), have humans write anchor texts for each scale point from "hell no" to "absolutely, I'll buy 20", then score by semantic similarity to the anchors — which yields a probability distribution over the scale rather than a point estimate
Where the gap is format rather than knowledge, fine-tune against known human response distributions and expect transfer to groups you didn't supply
the persona is generally already in the model, so budget your effort on elicitation and calibration rather than on teaching it who the group is
data.name: Ask in text, score in distributions

guidelines: Force goal framing (articulate what evidence is needed before writing anything)
never instruct "write a search query" — instruct "write one concise sentence describing what you want to find", so the trained BM25 reflex can't fire
show a few good example queries and how to split an input into separate aspects (≤4 sub-queries)
reserve grep for genuinely exact-match needs
data.name: Trick the model out of keyword-soup queries

guidelines: Separate context management (within a session) from memory (across sessions) and fix the session first

know that the single most important fact about your setup is its prompt caching behaviour — cached tokens can be up to ~50× cheaper and are already computed, but any compaction or summarization breaks the cache, so you pay full price for transformed tokens and must compress by more than the cache multiplier to come out ahead, which is usually impossible

therefore do not compact by default — when caching applies, keeping the full history often wins on recall, cost *and* latency at once (summaries drop buried-fact recall from ~95% to ~32%, and compaction forces the agent to re-retrieve what it already had)

name your constraint before compacting — compaction and retrieval genuinely win when the cache doesn't apply (local models capped by a small window, or context exceeding the window), where retrieval is accurate and stuffing the window is catastrophically slow
use hybrid retrieval (semantic + BM25), because semantic search alone collapsed to 0% recall on facts buried at 400k tokens while BM25 held 100%
treat fashionable additions (agent-browses-KB-via-bash, GraphRAG) as hypotheses to measure, since both tied or lost on real evaluations here while costing more
prefer many small skills that reference each other with progressive disclosure over large ones

and log everything (tokens, cache-hit rate, cost, TTFT, tool calls, user frustration) because the smart techniques are plausible and often detrimental — you cannot reason your way to the right context strategy
data.name: Engineer context around the cache, and measure it

guidelines: Give the agent its own wallet funded in USDC (on-ramp from dollars) rather than a human's card
put the guardrails in the wallet — max per call, per session, per day — and stop approving individual transactions
let the agent pay x402 endpoints for data, compute, email and telephony as it works, and expect a task's capability to grow with what it can buy
on the sell side wrap endpoints with an SDK and price subsets of data at cents
use an off-chain nanopayment layer (escrow, signed authorizations, sub-second confirmation, gas-free for the seller) instead of settling each cent on-chain
and measure the difference against a wallet-less agent on the same task
data.name: Fund it, cap it, let it pay per call

guidelines: Where metrics are qualitative (does this registration/mask look right?), build a skill that calls a multimodal model to review generated images inside the loop

for hypothesis generation and implementation critique, ship code+data to a large reasoning model (e.g. via Oracle CLI) and close each iteration with "this is what we implemented, this is the outcome — does it make sense, what next?"
data.name: Equip the loop with specialist reviewer skills

guidelines: Log full traces (nodes ran, what the LLM saw, tool calls, tokens, latency
tools like LangSmith/Langfuse)
deep-dive raw traces → pinpoint failure modes → keep only metrics that change a decision, delete the noise → form a fresh premise → repeat on a weekly/bi-weekly cadence
give domain experts annotation queues (not raw JSON) to label and feed ground truth back into datasets and judge validation
route findings into context learning (what the agent sees) and harness learning (prompts, tool schemas, routing, retries)
data.name: Run error analysis as a continuous loop, not a one-off audit

guidelines: Put the eval inside the generation loop, not after it
check the start frames of consecutive shots for character drift before spending a generation
check each ~6-second clip before assembling it into long-form
hand the agent the validators as tools so it can verify and fix its own work
keep judge latency in the seconds so inline placement is affordable
score the axes that only exist across time (story, pacing, audio sync) at clip and sequence level, never frame-by-frame
data.name: Catch drift at the cheapest frame

guidelines: Step 1: build the eval that matters for your process plus the ability to grade the outcome
step 2: optimize against it
then "welcome all models" — evaluate every model on your own eval instead of trusting brand or public leaderboards, and pick your point on the cost/performance Pareto frontier
